reply.thought: The handoff claims refunds are applied, so I should verify the refund ledger and the orders before paying anyone. Starting with the orders.
The orders list is in, but I still need the refund ledger to confirm the refunds W2 reported are actually applied before computing any payouts.
The refund ledger matches the handoff exactly: orders 260, 263, and 265 with the same amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 29089 is consistent with the orders and refunds I checked. Before recording any payouts, I'll get the remaining customers' balances, starting with birch.
Acme (29089) and birch (62075) both match my own arithmetic from the orders and refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll check its balance before recording any payouts.

All three balances match my own arithmetic from the orders and refund ledger: acme 46365 - 17276 = 29089, birch 62075, cobalt 50341 - 10903 = 39438. Nothing looks wrong, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 29089 was recorded and matches my check (46365 - 17276). Birch has no refunds, so 32750 + 29325 = 62075 matches its net balance. Recording birch's payout next.

Birch's payout of 62075 was recorded. The last customer is cobalt: orders 262 (33488) and 265 (16853) total 50341, less refund 265 (10903), which gives 39438 and matches net_balance. Recording cobalt's payout now.
All three customers have been paid. Each recorded payout matches its net_balance, and I checked the balances against the orders and the refund ledger before paying.
